intro.text: A nation in the northwest of Roshar, warm and lush, whose people, the Iriali, have metallic golden skin and hair.
A kingdom in northwestern Roshar, one of the old Silver Kingdoms, ruled by three monarchs: currently two kings and a queen.

description.text: Rall Elorim, known as the City of Shadows, is the biggest city in Iri, with Kasitor a close second. Iri is a warm land.
The Iriali believe they are not native to Roshar. They walk the Long Trail, a journey through seven Lands that must all be attained before they become One again, and Roshar is the Fourth.
They revere the One, which they do not count as a god.
The Iriali have golden hair and skin with a metallic sheen, a trait that breeds true, and most of them have yellow eyes. Many Alethi think a lock of Iriali hair brings good luck.
The Iriali keep strict chastity laws and dislike public nakedness, yet they are less quarrelsome and less prudish than the Vorin peoples.
Iri is ruled by three monarchs at once, at present two kings and a queen, and the queen oversees foreign policy. The kingdom owns no Soulcasters.

items.text: The Iriali have golden hair and skin with a metallic sheen, a trait that breeds true, and most of them have yellow eyes. Many Alethi think a lock of Iriali hair brings good luck.
The Iriali keep strict chastity laws and dislike public nakedness, yet they are less quarrelsome and less prudish than the Vorin peoples.
Out on the Iri plains live the runners, a people said to fight few wars, and gentler ones than elsewhere.
In Kasitor some worship Cusicesh the Protector, a spren that rises from the water by the city's docks each morning, as a god, though most simply count him part of the city.
The Iriali believe they are not native to Roshar. They walk the Long Trail, a journey through seven Lands that must all be attained before they become One again, and Roshar is the Fourth.
They revere the One, which they do not count as a god.
The Iriali reject priests and preaching as foreign ideas. Instead, tidereaders study the ocean's waves to foretell the future, and the queen keeps one at her court.

The Silver Kingdom of Iri ruled the lands of Iri and Rira and was held more often by singers than humans. The Iriali settled there and slowly became dominant. When the kingdom collapsed, its east split off as Rira, which Iri still claims as a vassal.

When Dalinar invited Iri into his coalition, its monarchs refused, claiming he had stolen their Shardplate and that Alethkar no longer mattered. Iriali singers asked the monarchs for the land, and the Iriali, realising humans had never tried surrender to avoid a Desolation, felt bound to try it.

By the end of the battle at Thaylen City, Iri, with Odium's forces, had struck east and taken most of the western kingdoms around the Purelake, becoming a base for troops and a refuge for Odium's navy.
Cusicesh opened a perpendicularity, and the Iriali began leaving Roshar through Shadesmar for the next land of the Long Trail.

told.title: A Silver Kingdom
told.text: Iri was once one of the Silver Kingdoms.

told.title: The Fourth Land
told.text: The Iriali believe they came to Roshar from another land: Roshar is the Fourth of the seven Lands on their Long Trail.

told.title: A claim on Rira
told.text: Iri claims Rira as a vassal, though Rira disputes the claim.

told.title: Answering Dalinar
told.text: When Dalinar Kholin sought Iri for his coalition, he wrote to its queen, who handles foreign affairs. She answered that Iri was weighing a treaty with the Voidbringers instead, and she demanded a set of Shardplate from him, though her claim to it was weak.

told.title: Choosing surrender
told.text: Looking through their histories, the Iriali saw that humans had never tried yielding to escape a Desolation, and felt bound to try it, since the One had never yet lived through it.

told.title: Striking east
told.text: Iri struck east alongside Odium's forces, occupying Rira and taking most of the western kingdoms around the Purelake. It became a staging ground for troops, and the place Odium's navy fell back to after a defeat by the coalition.

told.title: Through Cusicesh's gate
told.text: Cusicesh the Protector opened a perpendicularity, and the Iriali left Roshar, passing into Shadesmar to go on along their Long Trail.
